Subject: Thanks — quick follow-ups on throughput / latency

Thanks Rafael / Marissa —

Great call today. A couple quick follow-ups so we can size roughly for our procurement team:

1) Latency SLOs: Our product team wants 95th percentile generation latency under 400ms for single-turn chat (avg 300 tokens output, input ~80 tokens). For streaming responses, we want first-byte < 120ms and steady token emission at ~25-30 tokens/sec. Can Redwood meet this on a 8-12 token chunk streaming approach?

2) Throughput patterns: Typical steady-state: ~120 QPS of short interactive queries (avg 200 tokens total). Peak traffic: 800 QPS for 10-15 minute bursts during batch jobs (higher concurrency, many simultaneous sessions). We also have nightly ingestion jobs that will do high-volume embedding calls (~10k requests over an hour).

3) Concurrency / batching: Curious how Redwood recommends handling concurrency for streaming vs non-streaming, and what batching impact on latency we should expect.

4) Model profile: We plan to run an Llama-2-70B-v2 style open model (quantized) for chat, with ~8k context for some users. Wondering about KV cache sizing and memory implications.

Please confirm any obvious blockers and if you can share a rough tokens/sec and cost estimate for both steady-state and peak. Attaching our preliminary model profile (csv) — feel free to ignore if noisy.

Thanks —
Samir
Head of Platform
FinEx Payments

From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Thanks — quick follow-ups on throughput / latency

Samir —

Thanks for the clear summary and the model profile — super helpful. High level takeaways from our side:

- Latency SLOs: 95p < 400ms for single-turn with ~300 tokens output is achievable on Dedicated pools with the right GPU class (A100/RTX 6000 equivalent or better) and aggressive batching disabled for low-latency routes. For streaming first-byte <120ms we can hit that at low concurrency; sustained token emission at 25-30 tokens/sec is typical for GPU-backed streaming with optimized kernels.

- Throughput: Your steady-state (~120 QPS, ~200 tokens) maps roughly to X tokens/sec: 120 QPS * 200 tokens = 24k tokens/sec sustained. Peaks of 800 QPS would be ~160k tokens/sec for short bursts. Those numbers matter for cluster sizing and whether we recommend Dedicated capacity or hosted with burst tiers.

- Concurrency & batching: For interactive low-latency routes we recommend per-request concurrency limits and small max-batch sizes (1-4) to avoid tail latency increases. For batch/ingestion workloads, large batch sizes and KV cache reuse dramatically improve throughput. We can expose multiple routes: interactive (low-latency, low batch) and batch (high-throughput, high batch).

- Context/KV cache: 8k context with a 70B model increases memory/KV cache pressure. If you use quantized 8-bit weights plus a keyed KV cache, we’ll need to factor in memory for both model and cache. We’ll include rough VM/GPU sizing in the matrix attached.

Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll run an internal sizing worksheet and send a latency/SLA matrix with recommended cluster sizes and cost bands (steady vs peak).
2) Schedule a short deep-dive with Marissa (our infra/benchmark lead) to validate streaming numbers and concurrency assumptions.
3) You share a representative request log (anonymized) or a small synthetic traffic file so we can run a quick perf sim.

I attached our latency/SLA matrix and a short set of assumptions. Notes inline on the CSV look useful.

Thanks — happy to jump on another call this week if helpful.

— Rafael Mendes

Looping in some quick capacity/tech notes (from infra benching):

- Tokens/sec estimates are very model/hardware specific. For a 70B quantized model on an A100-80GB class GPU we typically see ~60-80K decode tokens/sec per GPU under favorable conditions (large batches). For low-latency interactive via small batches, expect ~4-12K tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length and attention compute.

- Based on Rafael's arithmetic: steady-state (~24k tokens/sec) could be handled by 2-6 GPUs in low-latency config (higher count if you need redundancy/az spread). Peak bursts (~160k tokens/sec) would need an autoscaled fleet or Dedicated pool with burst capacity ~3-4x baseline (so ~8-12 GPUs) depending on acceptable queuing.

- Streaming: first-byte target is largely dependent on call setup + model warm cache. Warm KV cache + pinned instances get you sub-100ms first byte more reliably. Cold starts add ~200-400ms.

- Concurrency guidance: set per-instance concurrent streams to limit (e.g., 8-16) for streaming routes to avoid token emission stalls. For non-streaming throughput endpoints, higher concurrency with batching gives much better throughput.

Action items for sizing call:
- Samir: share 24-72h sample traffic (anonymized) + example payloads (avg tokens in / out, 95p length).
- Rafael/Marissa: we'll produce a 2-tier recommendation (steady vs peak) with cost estimates and GPU counts.

Happy to block 30 mins tomorrow for the deep-dive.

— Marissa Cole
